subject: Logging hygiene and sensitive header redaction — decision matrix & demo request
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@healthsync.com>, security@healthsync.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-05-18T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Logging hygiene and sensitive header redaction — post-call recap

Hi Lena / HealthSync security team,

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on scope and who does what: 

Summary of ask
- HealthSync needs strong controls for request/response logs produced by Redwood-inference endpoints: ability to redact or pseudonymize headers (trace IDs, cookies), optionally strip full request bodies for PII, and enforce configurable retention windows per environment.
- Primary compliance drivers: SOC 2 + healthcare-data handling policies; audit team will need examples of redacted logs and a retention proof point.

What we covered on the call
- Options for redaction: header-level masking, deterministic hashing for trace IDs, complete suppression of request/response bodies for regulated routes.
- Runtime knobs: per-route sampling, prefix/KV caching trade-offs, and audit-export hooks.
- Residency and retention: logs can be routed to US-only audit streams and retention policies applied at the export layer.

Proposed next steps (action items)
1) I’ll share a decision matrix (attached) that maps your typical endpoints to recommended redaction strategy (mask/hash/strip) and estimated latency/cost impact.
2) HealthSync security to confirm 3 sample endpoint types you want included in a short PoC (api/login, api/claims, api/eligibility suggested).
3) We’ll schedule a 45-minute PoC demo where we show: live redaction rules, an audit-export with sample redacted snippets, and retention configuration.
4) We’ll provide an “audit snippet” (attached) — small text file showing before/after redaction to include in your SOC evidence folder.

Timing
- I can deliver the matrix + sample snippets by EOD tomorrow (5/19). If you confirm the three endpoints by end of day 5/19 we can schedule a PoC for the week of 5/27.

Open questions for HealthSync
- Do you require reversible pseudonymization (able to re-identify) or irreversible hashing?
- Any internal rules about preserving trace IDs for incident correlation vs. removing them entirely?

Attachments: redaction-decision-matrix.xlsx (matrix + tradeoffs), sample-audit-snippet.txt (before/after examples)

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Solutions 
Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0128
From: Lena Park <lena.park@healthsync.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@healthsync.com
Date: 2029-05-18T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Logging hygiene and sensitive header redaction — post-call recap

Vanessa — thanks, this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) For PHI workflows we prefer irreversible pseudonymization for exported audit artifacts (irreversible hashing) but in our internal incident pipeline we need deterministically hashed trace IDs so we can correlate events. So we need both behaviors depending on export target.
2) Retention: standard logs retained 30 days, audit exports 7 years. We’ll need to know whether Redwood can write to a segregated audit stream with its own retention policy.
3) For the PoC endpoints: we’ll pick api/login, api/claims, and api/eligibility — I’ll send the exact paths and one example payload by EOD tomorrow.

Can you confirm that the decision matrix will call out which options preserve trace correlation vs. which break it? Also: any preference on how we handle sampling during peak traffic (we saw ~12k rps at peak in the test env)?

—Lena
Lena Park
Director, Information Security 
HealthSync
lena.park@healthsync.com
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@healthsync.com>, security@healthsync.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-05-19T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Logging hygiene and sensitive header redaction — decision matrix & PoC scheduling

Lena — perfect, thanks for the details. Confirmations and next steps below.

Short answers
- Decision matrix: yes — each row will explicitly state whether the option preserves deterministic correlation (yes/no), whether it supports reversible re-id, and the estimated token/latency impact.
- Segregated audit stream: yes — we can push a filtered, redacted copy to a US-only audit stream with 7-year retention. That stream can be configured to only contain irreversible-hashed or fully-stripped artifacts per route.
- Sampling under high RPS: we’ll include guidance — recommended approach is adaptive sampling + sticky correlation keys for critical transactions (so you keep correlation while lowering total export volume).

Attached: redaction-decision-matrix.xlsx (mapping + recommended defaults) and sample-audit-snippet.txt (small before/after).

Proposed PoC schedule options (45 min)
- Tue 2029-05-28 10:00–10:45 PT
- Wed 2029-05-29 14:00–14:45 PT

Please confirm preferred slot and I’ll calendar and include a short runbook.

Internal notes (for Karthik & Monica):
- Karthik: we should prepare a quick demo script that toggles between: header-mask (trace id hashed), header-strip (trace id removed), and full-body suppression. Show effects on correlation and latency numbers.
- Monica: please prepare the audit-export pipeline (US-only S3 target) with a retention flag and sample lifecycle policy; we’ll need to hand off the sample to HealthSync for SOC evidence.

Thanks — I’ll block both slots tentatively until we hear back.

Vanessa
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-05-20T10:00:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Logging hygiene and sensitive header redaction — decision matrix & demo request (internal follow-up)

Forwarding HealthSync confirmation pending. Key internal tasks and owners: 

- Karthik: demo script + flag toggles (mask/hash/strip) + capture 95th p99 latency delta per toggle. Keep windows small (real-time demo, show data only for sample routes).
- Monica: provision US-only audit S3 bucket, lifecycle rule = 7 years retention -> Glacier Deep Archive after 180 days; provide ARN and sample lifecycle policy doc. Ensure we attach the sample-audit-snippet.txt produced by the demo to the HubSpot record.
- Also: prepare a short note on reversible vs irreversible pseudonymization trade-offs for legal. I’ll coordinate with HealthSync on which routes need reversible re-id in their internal incident pipeline.

I’ve tentatively scheduled Tue 5/28 10:00 PT for the PoC; if that conflicts let me know and I’ll move.

Thanks,
Vanessa
